ai.literal: Compassion wealth [is] wealth among wealth; material wealth base people with-even exist.
ai.translation: The wealth of compassion is the true wealth among all wealth. Material wealth exists even with the base.
ai.modern: அருளாகிய செல்வமே செல்வங்களில் சிறந்த செல்வமாகும். பொருளாகிய செல்வம் இழிந்தவர்களிடத்திலும் இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts two types of wealth: the wealth of compassion and material wealth. It declares that compassion is the ultimate wealth among all forms of wealth. This is because material wealth is common and can be found even among base or low-minded people. The word 'கண்ணும்' (even at the place of) emphasizes that possessing material goods does not indicate a person's true worth. Therefore, true value lies only in cultivating a compassionate heart.

ai.literal: Good by the path having sought, compassion let one maintain; many by ways even if examined, that itself is support.
ai.translation: Seek the good path and maintain compassion. Even if you examine many different ways, compassion alone is your true support.
ai.modern: நல்ல வழியை ஆராய்ந்து அருளைப் போற்றி வாழ்க. பல வழிகளிலும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தாலும் அந்த அருளே வாழ்க்கைக்குத் துணையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises the reader to seek the right path and cultivate compassion. The poet asserts that even if one explores many different philosophies or ways of life, compassion remains the only true support. The word 'ஆறு' means path or way, contrasting the single good path of grace with the multitude of other paths one might examine.

ai.literal: Compassion joined to those with hearts there is not darkness joined painful world entering.
ai.translation: Those whose hearts are joined with compassion will never enter the painful world of darkness.
ai.modern: அருள் பொருந்திய நெஞ்சத்தை உடையவர்களுக்கு இருள் சூழ்ந்த துன்ப உலகத்தில் நுழையும் நிலை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two states of being: a heart filled with compassion and a world filled with dark suffering. The word 'சேர்ந்த' (joined) is used twice to emphasize this contrast. Those who have joined their hearts with compassion are protected from joining or entering the dark, painful world. The 'dark world' represents a state of ignorance and suffering that naturally follows a lack of empathy.

ai.literal: enduring life having protected compassion to those who practice is not they say one's own life fearing deed
ai.translation: They say there are no fearful consequences for the lives of those who protect other living beings and practice compassion.
ai.modern: நிலைபெற்ற பிற உயிர்களைப் பாதுகாத்து அருள் உள்ளத்தோடு வாழ்பவர்களுக்கு, தம்முடைய உயிர் அஞ்சும்படியான துன்பச் செயல்கள் இல்லை என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that practicing compassion towards others is the ultimate protection for oneself. The phrase 'man uyir ompi' means protecting the enduring lives of all beings, while 'arul alvarkku' refers to those who actively practice compassion. The text asserts that such people will never encounter deeds ('vinai') that cause their own lives to fear ('tan uyir ancum'). By shielding others from harm, a compassionate person naturally shields their own life from fearful consequences.

ai.literal: Sorrow, compassion to those who possess, is not; wind moving fertile great world witness.
ai.translation: There is no sorrow for those who possess compassion. The vast, fertile world where the wind blows stands as witness to this.
ai.modern: அருளைப் போற்றி வாழ்பவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை. காற்று வீசுகின்ற வளமான இந்தப் பெரிய உலகமே இதற்குச் சாட்சியாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet declares that those who live with compassion will never experience deep sorrow or affliction. To prove this universal truth, the poet points to the vast, fertile world where the wind blows. The continuous existence and flourishing of this world serve as a living witness that a life of compassion protects one from suffering. The phrase 'வளி வழங்கும் மல்லன்மா ஞாலம்' (the great, fertile world where the wind moves) emphasizes the enduring and life-sustaining nature of the world, which mirrors the life-sustaining power of compassion.

ai.literal: Wealth having-departed they-who-forgot, they-will-say, compassion having-departed evil-deeds having-done those-who-conduct-themselves.
ai.translation: The wise say that those who abandon compassion and live doing evil are like those who have lost their wealth and forgotten themselves.
ai.modern: அருளை விட்டு விலகித் தீய செயல்களைச் செய்து வாழ்பவர்களை, தம் செல்வத்தை இழந்து அறிவை மறந்தவர்கள் என்று சான்றோர் கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the loss of compassion to the loss of wealth and awareness. Those who abandon compassion ('அருள்') and commit evil deeds ('அல்லவை') are described as people who have lost their wealth ('பொருள்') and fallen into forgetfulness ('பொச்சாந்தார்'). By using the same word 'நீங்கி' (having departed) for both compassion and wealth, the poet emphasizes that a life without compassion is as destitute and confused as a life ruined by the loss of all material security. Thus, doing evil is a sign of having forgotten one's true human nature.

ai.literal: Grace to those without, that world is not; wealth to those without, this world having become non-existent, like.
ai.translation: Just as this world is not for those without wealth, that world is not for those without grace.
ai.modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு இந்த உலகத்து வாழ்க்கை எப்படி இல்லையோ, அதுபோலவே அருள் இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு அந்த உலகத்து வாழ்க்கை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a direct parallel between material and spiritual well-being. Earthly life, referred to as 'this world', requires wealth to thrive and be meaningful. Similarly, 'that world', which denotes the higher spiritual realm or the fruits of a virtuous life, cannot be attained without grace and compassion. The comparative word 'āṅku' links the two conditions, emphasizing that a lack of compassion makes spiritual elevation just as impossible as poverty makes earthly comfort.

ai.literal: Wealth-lacking-people will-flourish one-time; grace-lacking-people are-ruined, again becoming is-rare.
ai.translation: Those without wealth may flourish one day, but those without compassion are utterly ruined; for them to prosper again is impossible.
ai.modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவர்கள் ஒரு காலத்தில் வளம் பெறலாம்; ஆனால் அருள் இல்லாதவர்கள் முற்றிலும் அழிந்தவர்களே, அவர்கள் மீண்டும் சிறப்படைவது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the loss of material wealth with the loss of compassion. Those who lose their wealth ('பொருளற்றார்') might regain it and flourish ('பூப்பர்') at some point ('ஒருகால்'). However, those who lack compassion ('அருளற்றார்') are truly ruined ('அற்றார்'). For them to recover or prosper again ('மற்று ஆதல்') is exceedingly rare or impossible ('அரிது'). The repetition of 'அற்றார்' emphasizes the finality of the spiritual ruin caused by a lack of grace.

ai.literal: He who is confused true reality having seen like that indeed if examined he who lacks compassion doing virtue.
ai.translation: If examined, the virtue practiced by one who lacks compassion is like a confused mind perceiving true reality.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், இரக்கம் இல்லாதவன் செய்யும் அறச்செயல்கள், மனத்தெளிவு இல்லாதவன் உண்மையான பொருளைக் கண்டதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a person without compassion trying to practice virtue to a confused person trying to grasp the ultimate truth. Just as a clouded mind cannot truly perceive reality, a heart without compassion cannot genuinely perform virtuous deeds. The word 'தெருளாதான்' (one lacking mental clarity) perfectly mirrors 'அருளாதான்' (one lacking emotional grace), showing that compassion is the fundamental clarity of the heart.

ai.literal: Before stronger ones oneself let think, oneself than weaker ones upon going at the time.
ai.translation: When advancing against those weaker than oneself, one should imagine oneself standing before those who are stronger.
ai.modern: தன்னை விட மெலிந்தவர்கள் மேல் தான் அதிகாரம் செலுத்தச் செல்லும் போது, தன்னை விட வலியவர்கள் முன் தான் அஞ்சி நிற்கும் நிலையை ஒருவன் நினைத்துப் பார்க்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches compassion by asking us to put ourselves in the shoes of the vulnerable. When a person is about to use their power against someone weaker, they are told to pause. In that moment, they should imagine themselves standing before someone much stronger. By remembering their own fear and helplessness in the face of greater power, they will naturally feel mercy toward those they are about to harm.
